share.said:
Lent events (port 62787) to everyone in your groups, as many at once as want it. To let fewer in at once, change it on your home page, or `svrngs share 62787 --limit <number>`.
svrngs is running here already, so they can open it now.
`svrngs unshare events` stops lending it.
If events takes a password on each request, paste what it takes in its Authorization header, then press Enter (Enter alone for none):

bo.text:
Your groups

This page is yours, on this computer alone. On it you see your groups and who is in each, open what the people in them lend you, each in a tab of its own beside this page, open each group’s folder, make a group, make a link to invite someone or to add your phone or another computer, and choose how many people at once may use what this computer lends them.

A link works for a day, while this computer is on. Making one stops the last link you made letting anyone new in; everyone it let in stays.

A program on this computer, such as one you chat with a friend’s model in, reaches what is lent to you at the address beside it: its Copy button copies it, for you to paste where the program asks for an address.

The House

People: Cy, Bo, Sam

The House’s folder is on this computer at /tmp/events-shots/bo/svrngs/The House

Open this folder

Make a link to invite someone to The HouseMake a link to add your phone or another computer of yours

Open Sam’s events Copy its address for a program
Make a group

A name for the group: Your name in it: Make a group

What this computer lends

This computer lends nothing.

Your home page, the same address each time svrngs starts: http://svrngs.localhost:62706/

Done in a terminal

A few things are not done on this page yet. For each, open the Terminal app and type its line, with your own words in place of each <…>:

Lend your groups a program this computer runs, such as a model: svrngs share <the number after the colon in its address>, as in svrngs share 8080 for one at http://localhost:8080. svrngs then says what it lent, and to whom.
Remove someone from a group: svrngs remove <their name> --group <the group’s name>

Leaving a group is not possible yet: nothing in svrngs does it.
